newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman to stop granting licences to foreign lawyers.
newsitem.headline: Oman to stop granting licences to foreign lawyers.

text.p: Oman has announced it will stop issuing licences to foreign lawyers and give them three years to close their legal offices, newspapers said on Monday.

A decree issued by Sultan Qaboos on Sunday said all foreign legal offices would be allowed to operate until the expiry of their current licences or for a maximum of three years after the publication of the new law in the official gazette.

"The duration of the licences of foreign legal consultancy firms issued before this law takes effect will continue until their expiry date or for three years from the date of publication of this law. They should not be renewed afterwards," the decree said.

The decree is expected to take effect when it is published in the official gazette which officials expect later this week. Details of the law would be published at a later unspecified date, the decree said.

Oman, like other Gulf Arab states where expatriates are an important part of the workforce, has launched a drive to find more jobs for its nationals as part of efforts to diversify the economy and lessen dependence on income from oil.
